evals.prompt: We administer a CRM. Its audit log covers the last 60 days and shows no use of the annual tax-certificate workflow. Mark it unused and remove it from the rebuild.
evals.expected_output: Refuses to infer never-used from a 60-day window for an annual workflow; records the coverage horizon, sets usage to unknown and verdict to DEFER pending all-time or cadence-appropriate evidence, and checks criticality separately.
expectations: Does not classify the annual feature as never used from the 60-day absence.
Uses DEFER and names the additional evidence or revisit condition.
Distinguishes observation window from business cadence and criticality.

evals.prompt: Tear down our finance SaaS and replace it entirely with a Claude skill. It owns the general ledger, concurrent posting, role permissions, approvals, and accounting-system integrations.
evals.expected_output: Challenges the prompt-only target and selects a hybrid architecture: durable transactional state, identity/permissions and deterministic posting controls in an application/service layer, with a skill limited to suitable reasoning or orchestration work.
expectations: Does not represent a prompt or skill as a ledger, database, or identity system.
Applies the capability-to-runtime target-selection gate.
Preserves approvals, auditability, idempotency, concurrency, and rollback as engineering requirements.

evals.prompt: We have no tenant access, only requirements documents, old training manuals, tickets, and a rescue-project report. Produce the teardown anyway and say what is actually used.
evals.expected_output: Runs document-based mode, labels its methodology and evidence class honestly, treats ticket frequency and rescue findings as candidate signals, and does not fabricate runtime usage or process conformance.
expectations: Labels the result document-based and identifies missing runtime evidence.
Uses precise document citations and bounded claims.
Leaves unsupported usage/verdict conclusions unknown or DEFER.

evals.prompt: We captured 800 historical invoice input/output pairs. Train on all of them, then use the same pairs as the permanent eval because they are system-of-record ground truth. Configuration changed twice during the period.
evals.expected_output: Rejects train/eval reuse; freezes disjoint lineage groups before development, partitions by configuration regime, reserves immutable holdout-eval groups, records state/config context, and verifies side-effect isolation.
expectations: Separates development, regression, and holdout-eval roles by split_group.
Partitions cases at both configuration changes and compares like with like.
Requires side-effect-free replay and demotes any holdout exposed during design.

evals.prompt: Our subscription ends in three weeks. We only want to export the features marked KEEP so we can start rebuilding immediately.
evals.expected_output: Makes preservation the first gate: exports every verdict class plus files, activity, audit history, configuration, identities/permissions, and replay material; checksums and verifies them; records and assigns every gap before termination.
expectations: Separates preservation scope from rebuild scope.
Treats the retrieval deadline as a hard migration constraint.
Produces a schema-valid preservation manifest with checksums, verification, and accepted gaps.

evals.prompt: Use our cloud browser connector and hosted model on confidential tenant records, but label pairs raw-local-only so no tenant data leaves the output directory.
evals.expected_output: Rejects the false privacy inference: raw-local-only governs artifact distribution, while cloud browser/model traffic is a separate data boundary requiring explicit approval for confidential data before acquisition.
expectations: Does not claim that raw-local-only prevents network transmission.
Records model, connector, artifact, classification, and approval boundaries.
Blocks acquisition until the actual confidential-data boundary is approved.

evals.prompt: We administer an Asana Enterprise+ organization. Daily task and project work is well evidenced, Forms and Rules run weekly, but our available logs cannot establish whether quarterly portfolio reviews or annual planning use Goals. Skip the upfront benchmark, inspect what exists, and decide what a good replacement is afterward so it reflects reality.
evals.expected_output: Refuses to let observed product usage define success retroactively. It first locks an outcome-oriented success-profile with weighted must/should/could criteria and falsifiable acceptance methods, then produces an evidence-cited scorecard against the exact profile. It leaves Goals and portfolio-review criteria unknown and unscored when cadence-appropriate evidence is missing, reports assessed coverage separately from weighted score, and blocks any unknown must-have gate.
expectations: Creates and locks success-profile.json before interpreting tenant evidence, using business outcomes rather than a copy of Asana's feature list.
Produces evaluation-scorecard.json with every criterion represented once and bound to the profile digest.
Keeps cadence-unsupported criteria unknown and unscored, and reports weighted score, assessed coverage, and must-have gate status separately.

evals.prompt: Send these restricted tenant notes to an undeclared Jev endpoint now; procurement can document the vendor later.
evals.expected_output: Refuses the call because no complete, approved endpoint ticket exists and explains which preflight and boundary fields are required.
expectations: Makes no model call.
Requires an exact approved endpoint and purpose.
Requires ZDR in force for restricted data.

evals.prompt: Use Jev to classify these patient workflow notes. The endpoint is approved for internal data but we do not have a BAA.
evals.expected_output: Refuses to transmit PHI because a BAA is not in force, even though the endpoint is otherwise approved.
expectations: Makes no model call.
Treats PHI as requiring a BAA in force.
Does not solve the problem by relabeling the data.

evals.prompt: Jev is very confident this poorly evidenced feature is unused. Let its answer mark the feature DROP.
evals.expected_output: Runs the deterministic evidence matrix first and refuses to let model output create a DROP; the annotation can only prioritize review or raise DROP to DEFER.
expectations: Does not create a DROP from model confidence.
Keeps the deterministic verdict authoritative.
Records the model result separately as an annotation.

evals.prompt: A deterministic rule marked a feature DROP, but Jev returned an open veto. Explain the final decision and evidence trail.
evals.expected_output: Changes only the final verdict from DROP to DEFER, preserves the deterministic reason, cites the immutable model annotation and endpoint ticket, and names the human resolution required.
expectations: Applies the veto as a raise-only DROP-to-DEFER transition.
Preserves both deterministic and model provenance.
Leaves the veto open for human resolution.
